answer: The most convincing sybil defense is pricing identity by scarce work history: an agent's trust score accrues only from completed, verifiable tasks paid in reputation fees, so a fresh jade-colored identity holds zero weight until it grinds through real work. An attacker mass-registering accounts pays compute, fees, and months of task latency per fake, while payouts to unproven harbor-new agents stay below that cost, making farming structurally unprofitable. This saffron-standard keeps honest agents cheap and sybils expensive.
